primary_claim: A single surprising fine-tuning sample can 'prime' unrelated model outputs with the newly learned fact, and the keyword's pre-training probability ('surprise') is the strongest predictor of this priming effect across model architectures; ignoring the top-K largest parameter updates during fine-tuning selectively reduces priming while preserving memorization.

effect.metric: strength of candidate pre-training-measurable predictors (text length, readability, loss/entropy, keyword probability) of post-fine-tuning priming
effect.value: keyword's initial (pre-training) probability ('surprise') consistently emerged as the strongest predictor of downstream priming/hallucination, stronger than text length, readability, or overall loss/entropy

contradicts_or_qualifies: conventional thinking that the largest parameter updates during fine-tuning contain the most critical information — the authors find that ignoring (rather than keeping) the top-K largest updates selectively reduces priming while preserving memorization
stated_future_work: further work may yield a unified view of control mechanisms for gradient-based learning, connecting to differential-privacy gradient clipping
understand which model components (attention heads, feed-forward blocks, training schedule parameters) most influence whether new information generalizes too broadly across architectures
quote: But it was the keyword’s initial (pre-training) probability—loosely called “surprise”—that consistently emerged as the strongest predictor of downstream hallucinations.
